journey.name: paykit swap restore
journey.description:
Proves that a swap route the wallet left in flight before its claim is finished after the wallet is wiped and restored from its recovery phrase: the restore finds the swap at its provider, claims it to Savings (the contact's address does not survive the restore), and tells the user the payment was returned to Savings.
Preconditions: as paykit-swap-route.xml, with the provider running against bitkit-docker (`--no-homeserver`) and the build's PUBKY_SWAPS_PROVIDERS naming it. A throwaway regtest wallet restored from a recovery phrase, with a spending balance from an LNURL channel, an empty savings balance, a Pubky profile, and the provider and the fixture-issuer saved as contacts. Start a 20 000 sat payment to the fixture-issuer through the swap route, wait until the provider logs "HTLC funded; awaiting client claim", and force-stop the app before any block is mined. Then clear the app's data and enter the same recovery phrase on the restore screen.

actions.action: Tap Restore (tag "RestoreButton") and wait for the Wallet Restored screen, then tap Get Started (tag "GetStartedButton")
Mine one block on bitkit-docker's bitcoind, so the provider's lockup confirms
Verify the provider logs "client claimed; hold invoice settled"
Mine one more block, so the claim confirms
Verify the "Received Bitcoin" sheet shows 20 000, then close it
Verify the toast "Payment returned to Savings" is visible
Verify the savings balance (tag "ActivitySavings") shows 20 000, and bitcoind shows the claim transaction paying exactly 0.0002 BTC to the wallet's own address
